findings.title: Run step interpolates attacker-controlled GitHub event data
findings.description: User-submitted fields like PR titles, bodies, and comments can inject shell content into workflows.
findings.recommendation: Pass untrusted event data through actions that safely escape it, or treat it as data rather than shell code.
findings.evidence: Run step contains user input markers: `echo "${{ github.event.comment.body }}"`.

findings.title: Workflow uses pull_request_target
findings.description: `pull_request_target` runs in the base repository context and has been a recurring root cause in CI/CD compromise chains.
findings.recommendation: Avoid `pull_request_target` for code from forks. Prefer `pull_request`, or isolate privileged jobs behind a separate trusted workflow.

findings.title: Job or workflow grants broad write permissions
findings.description: Over-permissioned GitHub tokens increase blast radius when a workflow is compromised.
findings.recommendation: Reduce permissions to the narrowest required set and keep write scopes off untrusted execution paths.

findings.title: Untrusted workflow runs on a self-hosted runner
findings.description: Self-hosted runners in PR-style contexts let attacker-controlled code execute inside your infrastructure.
findings.recommendation: Keep self-hosted runners off untrusted events or isolate them behind manual approvals and strong network boundaries.
findings.evidence: Job `publish` uses self-hosted runners while workflow triggers include pull_request_target, workflow_dispatch.

findings.title: Publish job lacks OIDC trusted publishing posture
findings.description: Recent package compromises frequently depended on long-lived publish tokens stored as secrets.
findings.recommendation: Move publish jobs to OIDC trusted publishing for npm or PyPI and remove static registry credentials.
findings.evidence: Publish-style job `publish` does not request `id-token: write`.

findings.title: Publish job exposes long-lived registry or platform secrets
findings.description: Static package publish tokens are a primary target in modern supply-chain compromises.
findings.recommendation: Replace long-lived secrets with OIDC trusted publishing and rotate any exposed credentials.
findings.evidence: Publish job env includes: NPM_TOKEN=${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }} PYPI_API_TOKEN=${{ secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN }}

findings.title: Action is referenced by tag or branch instead of a full commit SHA
findings.description: Floating action references are a common supply-chain pivot because they can change without repository review.
findings.recommendation: Pin external actions to full-length commit SHAs and manage updates through Dependabot or controlled review.

findings.title: pull_request_target job checks out attacker-controlled PR head
findings.description: This pattern turns a privileged base-repo workflow into direct execution of untrusted code.
findings.recommendation: Do not combine `pull_request_target` with checkout of PR head content. Split trust boundaries into separate workflows.
findings.evidence: Checkout step references PR head in `actions/checkout@v4` with args `{'ref': '${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}'}`.

findings.title: Action is referenced by tag or branch instead of a full commit SHA
findings.description: Floating action references are a common supply-chain pivot because they can change without repository review.
findings.recommendation: Pin external actions to full-length commit SHAs and manage updates through Dependabot or controlled review.

findings.title: Run step interpolates attacker-controlled GitHub event data
findings.description: User-submitted fields like PR titles, bodies, and comments can inject shell content into workflows.
findings.recommendation: Pass untrusted event data through actions that safely escape it, or treat it as data rather than shell code.
findings.evidence: Run step contains user input markers: `echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"`.

repo_recommendations: Enable GitHub Actions workflow scanning and keep it mandatory on pull requests.
Move npm and PyPI publishing to OIDC trusted publishing where available.
Pin third-party actions to full commit SHAs and monitor updates deliberately.
Keep secrets and self-hosted runners away from untrusted PR execution paths.
